claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance and undergoes rapid high-temperature oxidation.
Pack cementation or an equivalent vapor-deposition treatment can produce a thin, diffusion-bonded, adherent aluminide layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminide layer will transform in situ into a continuous and adherent Al2O3 surface scale during high-temperature oxidation.
The aluminide coating will serve as an aluminum reservoir for formation of the Al2O3 scale.
A continuous Al2O3 scale will slow further oxygen ingress into the alloy.
The surface treatment will not alter the bulk microstructure governing ductility and yield strength.
The coated alloy will oxidize substantially more slowly than untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr at 1000 °C in air.
After coating and oxidation exposure, room-temperature tensile ductility will remain within 8–16%.
After coating and oxidation exposure, yield strength at 1000 °C will remain within 163–530 MPa.
The proposed application boundary is approximately 1000 °C in air for exposures of 100–200 hours and mechanical strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
An Al2O3- and TiC-containing NbMoCrTiAl composite has higher room-temperature compressive fracture strength than its as-cast NbMoCrTiAl reference alloy.

contradictions.description: The falsification rule treats any yield strength outside 163–530 MPa as degradation, although a value above 530 MPa would be an improvement rather than a loss of mechanical performance.
